report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of drift.py (check function): integrity checks, phantom-entry validation, island/unknown/shims classification, engine-disagreement, reached/vanished reporting.
risks: line 1121 | medium | _remedy(NOW_REACHED) returns a string that instructs the user to re-baseline (--refresh), but an accepted island is deliberately absent from the baseline; a NOW_REACHED item for a previously accepted island may not be bankable by --refresh because the acceptance is not recorded in the snapshot. | Inspect write_snapshot to see whether acceptances are stored; if not, the remedy is misleading for accepted islands.

line 1161 | medium | If stored_schema differs from SCHEMA_VERSION, the function returns a DriftReport with snapshot={} instead of the actual snapshot, which may drop information a caller expects. | Check whether callers rely on snapshot contents when schema mismatches.

line 1172 | medium | The digest check appends an INVALID_SNAPSHOT item but does not return early, so subsequent checks still run on a possibly tampered snapshot. This may be intentional (accumulate findings) but could produce confusing cascading errors. | Confirm whether the design intends to report all integrity failures at once.

line 1235 | medium | The phantom_test_only check uses old_islands | old_unknown | old_shims, but test_only modules are also unreached via the 'island' acceptance keys; an accepted island that is in test_only would be flagged as phantom even though it is a known unreached module. | Check whether accepted islands can appear in test_only in the snapshot.

line 1325 | medium | The loop for 'unknown' and 'shims' uses old_set & old_modules to compute baselined, but accepted islands are deliberately absent from the baseline; if an accepted island is in 'unknown' or 'shims', it will not be considered baselined and will be reported as NEW_UNKNOWN/NEW_SHIM, possibly duplicating the acceptance. | Check whether accepted islands can appear in unknown/shims lists.

handoff.purpose: Implementation of check(): validates snapshot integrity, detects phantom entries, classifies unreached modules, and reports drift findings.

symbols.name: check
symbols.note: Compares generated state against committed snapshot; may write a baseline snapshot when write_missing=True and snapshot is absent.

claims.text: A missing snapshot FAILS unless write_missing is set, which is the explicit "record a baseline" action rather than the default.
claims.why: Lines 1130-1134: if snapshot is None and write_missing is False, returns DriftReport(ok=False, first_run=True, ...). If write_missing is True, writes snapshot and returns ok=True.

claims.text: The previous default -- write it and report OK -- meant rm docs/architecture-state .json was a green run, and a green run against nothing is exactly what this file exists to make impossible.
claims.why: The default write_missing is False (parameter default), so missing snapshot now fails; the described previous behavior is no longer present.

claims.text: the mechanical lists do not match the digest written with them: something was hand-edited
claims.where: comment at line 1165, detail string at lines 1167-1169
claims.why: Lines 1165-1171 compare stored_digest to recomputed _digest(snapshot) and append INVALID_SNAPSHOT item when mismatch.

claims.text: Pre-seeding an item into 'islands' or 'dark_switches' is not a way to accept it -- an acceptance is dated and an acceptance is reviewed
claims.why: The code detects phantom islands (lines 1205-1212) and phantom dark switches (lines 1232-1239), reporting them as INVALID_SNAPSHOT. It does not treat them as acceptances.

claims.text: A count matching its own list proves only internal arithmetic. These check the lists against reality and against each other, so an entry cannot be pre-seeded to suppress a finding that has not landed yet.
claims.why: Phantom checks at lines 1205-1239 verify that islands/unknown/shims/test_only/dark_switches entries exist in the snapshot's own modules list or in the environment reads, preventing pre-seeding.

claims.text: every test-only module is an unreached module first
claims.why: Lines 1219-1226 check that each test_only entry is in old_islands | old_unknown | old_shims; otherwise it is flagged as phantom.

claims.text: a switch cannot be baselined before the code that reads it exists
claims.why: Lines 1232-1239 compare old_dark against read_names from result.switches.env_switches and flag any phantom entries as INVALID_SNAPSHOT.

claims.text: An accepted island is deliberately absent from the baseline (:func:`write_snapshot`), so the baseline alone would read it as "reached" and call it BECAME ISLAND the moment the module also appears in ``modules``.
claims.why: The claim about write_snapshot's behavior is in another function in this file; this chunk does not show write_snapshot. The logic in this chunk does use accepted_keys to compute known_unreached, which supports the claim's consequence.

claims.text: The acceptance is itself a record that it is an island, so it counts toward what the snapshot knows -- without suppressing anything.
claims.why: accepted_keys is built from acceptances (line 1244) and used to compute known_unreached (lines 1250-1252), so accepted islands are treated as known unreached without suppressing the island finding.

claims.text: Intersecting with ``modules`` is the teeth behind the subset rule above: an island entry the snapshot's own module list does not back is a hand-edit, and a hand-edit must not be able to suppress the finding it was written to hide.
claims.why: baselined_islands = old_islands & old_modules (line 1247) and phantom_islands check (lines 1205-1212) enforce that islands must be in modules; otherwise flagged as INVALID_SNAPSHOT.

claims.text: BECAME ISLAND means "it was REACHED and is not any more". A module the snapshot recorded as unknown or as an unreached shim was never reached, so it must not be described that way when it degrades into an island.
claims.why: known_unreached includes old_unknown and old_shims (line 1250), and was_reached is computed as mod in old_modules and mod not in known_unreached (line 1272), so unknown/shim modules are not reported as BECAME_ISLAND.

claims.text: Same shape as islands, deliberately not merged into them: the finding a reader gets has to say WHICH kind of unreached this is, because the three remedies are three different sentences.
claims.why: The loop at lines 1286-1315 handles unknown and shims separately, each with its own prefix and kind, and produces distinct DriftItem entries.

claims.text: What they share is the property that used to be missing entirely -- a module nothing reaches is COUNTED, is named, and blocks until somebody explains it.
claims.why: The loop reports each unknown/shim module as an item (lines 1306-1309) unless baselined or test-only, so the module is named and counted.

claims.text: It is reported, never merged: merging it is how a dead-branch import used to make its target 'reachable'
claims.why: Lines 1317-1322 report each new index edge as ENGINE_DISAGREEMENT item; there is no code that merges the edge into the reachability state.

claims.text: ``new_unreached``, not ``new_islands``: a module that moved from island to shim (or to unknown) is still reached by nothing, and announcing "something reaches it now" would be the same false-green in a new costume.
claims.why: Lines 1327-1331 check if mod not in new_unreached (which includes new_islands | new_unknown | new_shims), so a module that moved between unreached classes is not reported as NOW_REACHED.

observations.what: The NOW_REACHED remedy for an accepted island may be misleading because accepted islands are deliberately absent from the baseline; the remedy instructs to re-baseline, but the acceptance is not recorded in the snapshot.

The phantom_test_only check uses old_islands | old_unknown | old_shims, but accepted islands that are also in test_only would be flagged as phantom because accepted islands are absent from those lists.

The loop for unknown and shims uses old_set & old_modules to determine baselined, but accepted islands are deliberately absent from the baseline; if an accepted island appears in unknown or shims, it will not be considered baselined and will be reported as NEW_UNKNOWN/NEW_SHIM, potentially duplicating the acceptance.
